records.name: 3D object
records.description: Rotate and zoom into the model with simple gestures in 3D.

records.name: Add picture
records.description:
With this control users can take photos or upload image files from their device and update the data source with this content. On a mobile device the user is presented with the device's choice dialog to choose between taking a photo or selecting one already available.

This control is a grouped control containing two controls: an Image and an Add picture button. The Image control shows the uploaded image or a placeholder if no image has been uploaded. The Add picture button prompts for an image to be uploaded.

records.name: Address input
records.description:
Entering addresses can be frustrating and error-prone, particularly in mobile apps. Use the address input control to make address entry easier. The control uses fuzzy logic to suggest potential matches as you type. Select the one you want to quickly and easily enter an accurate address.

The control returns the address as structured data. Your app can extract information such as city, street, municipality, and even latitude and longitude coordinates. The data is in a format that's friendly to many locales and international address formats.

records.name: Attachments
records.description: A control that allows users to download files to their device, as well as upload and delete files from a list created using Microsoft Lists, or a Microsoft Dataverse table.

records.name: Audio
records.description: An Audio control plays a sound clip from a file, a recording from a Microphone control, or the audio track from a video file.

records.name: Avatar
records.description: Use the avatar control to visually represent a user, team, or entity. This control supports both image and initials formats and allows a small badge to be included to help convey status. The key properties for this control are Name and Image.

records.name: Badge
records.description: Badge can be used to display content in a visually better way. The key properties for this control are Content, Shape, and Appearance.

records.name: Barcode reader
records.description:
The control opens a native scanner on Android, iOS, and Windows devices. On iOS and Android, the scanner supports the following scanning modes:

- Automatically scan – A barcode is scanned as soon as it's detected.
- Select to scan – The user can determine which of the detected barcodes to scan. The control doesn't support scanning in a web browser.
- Scan multiple – The user can scan multiple barcodes during the barcode session.

On Windows devices, the barcode reader will always automatically scan.

The barcode reader control supports different zoom levels and turning on/off the device's flashlight from within the scanning experience.

records.name: Button
records.description: A control that the user can click or tap to interact with the app.

records.name: Button
records.description: Use the modern button to set a button to be primary or secondary. Configure the OnSelect property of a Button control to run one or more formulas when the user selects the control. The key properties for this control are OnSelect and Text.

records.name: Camera
records.description: Use the Camera control to capture pictures with a device's camera. The device must have a camera and the user must authorise the app to use the camera.

records.name: Card
records.description: The card control is a container for controls inside a form and is therefore exempt from accessibility assessment.

records.name: Checkbox
records.description: The user can specify a Boolean value by using this familiar control that is used in Graphical User Interface (GUI) for decades. The key properties for this control are Checked, Label, OnCheck, and OnUncheck.

records.name: Combo box
records.guidance: Contrast very low on guidance/status text, same issue as Address Picker. Menu experience for keyboard users is poor, arrow keys are used to navigate the drop down list but reaching the bottom of the list and pressing down again causes a loss of focus. Expected behaviour would be to loop back to the top of the menu or inform the user that this is the last item and retain focus. If this cannot be rectified in the config, guidance for keyboard and AT users should be present before they interact with this control to minimise frustration.

records.name: Copilot answer
records.description: Makers can use the Copilot answer control to set predefined questions that end users can use to get generative answers with a single click. The control is optimized for mobile users and is powered by Microsoft Copilot.

records.name: Data table
records.guidance: This control is in preview and has been for years. Do not use.

records.name: Date picker
records.description: Adding a Date Picker control instead of a Text input control ensures the user specifies a date in the correct format. The key properties for this control are Format, ValidationState, and OnChange.
records.guidance: Use multiple free text inputs with bounds instead, eg 1-12 for month 1-31 for day: Dates – GOV.UK Design System

records.name: Display form
records.guidance: This is a container. Accessibility will be determined by the contents, ensure everything within is accessible.

records.name: Drop down
records.guidance: Only use with short lists of options.

records.name: Dropdown
records.description: A Drop down control conserves screen real estate, especially when the list contains a large number of choices. The control takes up only one line unless the user selects the chevron to reveal more choices. The key properties for this control are Items, ValidationState, and OnChange.

records.name: Edit form
records.guidance: This is a container. Accessibility will be determined by the contents, ensure everything within is accessible.

records.name: Export
records.guidance: Not keyboard interactable.

records.name: Form
records.guidance: This is a container. Accessibility will be determined by the contents, ensure everything within is accessible.

records.name: Form Processor
records.guidance: Also known as AI Builder

records.name: Gallery
records.guidance: This is a container. Accessibility will be determined by the contents, ensure everything within is accessible.

records.name: Header
records.description: The Header control is a fundamental control that lets you design a user interface for a common app with ease. With minimal configuration, this control responds to themes that use modern theming and dynamic responsiveness, adjusting to the size of the parent container or app. The Header control supports a logo, a page title, and displays the user picture, while providing various unique style options. The key properties for this control are Logo, OnSelectLogo, and Title.
records.guidance: Use Header from our component library instead of this, or build your own if confident.

records.name: HTML text
records.guidance: This is a container. Accessibility will be determined by the contents, ensure everything within is accessible.

records.name: Icon
records.guidance: Ensure proper tab indexing or this control will not be keyboard/AT accessible.

records.name: Modern Icon
records.guidance: Ensure any information conveyed visually is also available in text format next to the icon.

records.name: List Box
records.guidance: Use checkboxes instead, if you need to use this control instead please contact the Power Platform team.

records.name: Number input
records.description: Makers can add a number input control to type in or use the arrows to select a number value. They can configure decimal precision and step values for this control. This control provides number type as a default output to build numeric scenarios in Power Apps. A key property for this control is Value.

records.name: PDF Viewer
records.guidance: This control is experimental! General accessibility guidance is to avoid PDFs where possible, if required for your application then ensure any embedded PDFs are as accessible as possible.

records.name: Pen Input
records.guidance: Mobile only

records.name: Pie Chart
records.guidance: All data for the chart must be displayed by default in an accessible format (text). If a visual representation is required, it must be on a separate screen to avoid adding extra steps to the focus order.

records.name: Power BI Tile
records.description: Display a Power BI tile inside an app.

records.name: Progress bar
records.description: The progress bar can be configured to show various states of progress in the apps. This versatile control can be used to inform users on their progress as they work on the app or can be used to show loading scenarios. The key properties for this control are Value, Max, and Indeterminate.
records.guidance: Control does not convey any information to screen reader users, can still be used but you must also have a classic text control to announce loading start and end done in a proper fashion to announce to screen readers.

records.name: Radio group
records.description: A Radio group control is best used with only a few, mutually exclusive options. The key properties for this control are Items and DefaultSelectedItems.
records.guidance: Not accessible for keyboard users. Use classic Radio control instead.

records.name: Rating
records.guidance: Up and down keyboard input functionality is reversed, use an alternative for ratings such as dropdown or radio buttons.

records.name: Slider
records.description: The user can indicate a value, between a minimum and a maximum value that you specify, by dragging the handle of a slider left-right or up-down, depending on the direction that you choose. The key properties for this control are OnChange, Value, Min, and Max.

records.name: Spinner
records.description: Spinner control can be used to display loading scenarios where an action is in progress. This powerful control provides multiple display options suited for many scenarios. The key properties for this control are Label, Appearance, and SpinnerSize.
records.guidance: Spinner control does not convey any information to screen reader users, can still be used but you must also have a classic text control to announce loading start and end done in a proper fashion to announce to screen readers.

records.name: Table
records.description: The Table control is a modern responsive control that shows a set of data in a tabular or list format. The tabular format includes column headings for each displayed field and a footer that provides details about the dataset such as the record count. The list format presents the data in a single column and has three fields for each row. As an app maker, you have full control over what fields are added to the control including the order. Although all added fields are visible in the tabular format

records.name: Tabs or tab list
records.description: A Tab is a navigation control, which can help users switch between different context within the app. You can add list of items to tabs or select a data table field for the list in tabs to appear. The key properties for this control are Items, OnChange, and OnSelect.
records.guidance:
For the horizontal layout, up and down arrow inputs break page focus. For the vertical layout, left arrow inputs break page focus.

 

Do not use if possible. If you must use, ensure there is guidance available for end users before they encounter this issue.

records.name: Text
records.description: Use this versatile Text control to display text, messages, and information on the app. The key properties for this control are Text, Size, and FontColor.
records.guidance: This text will not alert screen reader users if the content changes. If your text is dynamic or changes, use the classic text control instead.

records.name: Text input
records.description: The user can specify data by typing into a Text input control. Depending on how you configure the app, that data might be added to a data source, used to calculate a temporary value, or incorporated in some other way. The key properties for this control are Value, Mode, and ValidationState.
records.guidance: Users should ideally be able to see all the text that they have input without scrolling, please increase the size of the text box to match the expected input length.

records.name: Toggle
records.description: A toggle is a user interface element that has been created for modern graphical user interfaces (GUIs), but it functions in the same manner as a checkbox. The key properties for this control are Checked, Label, OnCheck, OnSelect, and OnUncheck.

records.name: Combobox
records.description: A Combobox control lets you present collections of items for users to select. Configure single or multi-select mode via the SelectMultiple property. Key properties for this control are Items, DefaultSelectedItems, SelectedItems, SelectMultiple, and IsSearchable.
records.guidance: Use classic control instead.

records.name: Link
records.description: Use Link control to provide links that can be defined with accessibility compliance. The link opens in a new tab on your device. The key properties for this control are Text and URL.

records.name: Information button
records.description: Info button control enables developers to provide help and guidance to app users in an accessible way. The key properties for this control are Content, Icon Size, and OnSelect.
records.guidance:
Ensure any information locked behind interaction with this control is also available as text next to the control.

 

[Retest with AT pending]

records.name: Stream
records.description: The Stream control in Power Apps lets you embed Microsoft Stream (on SharePoint) videos directly in your canvas app. Adding a Stream video in your app makes a smooth integration of videos hosted on Microsoft Stream in your canvas app. It also improves the user experience.
records.guidance: Do not use due to preview status, easier to link to video content.
